items.headline: Wind Advisory issued July 23 at 6:36AM AKDT until July 23 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 40 mph with gusts up to 60 mph.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
items.areas: Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued July 23 at 6:18AM AKDT until July 23 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Water levels 1 to 2 feet above the highest high tide
line.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur. Water will
approach the road to the Hooper Bay Airport, but should not
inundate the airport or the road.
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued July 23 at 4:12AM AKDT until July 23 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 25 to 40 mph with gusts of 50 to 65 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River Hillsides.

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT today.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result. The combination of saturated soils and
wind could also lead to downed trees, especially already damaged
or diseased trees.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 22 at 2:43PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Water levels will rise slightly with each high tide Wednesday
night through Friday morning. The highest water level rises will
be in Eastern Norton Sound, around 1 to 3 feet above the normal
high tide line. Water level rises around 0.5 to 1.5 feet are
expected from Golovin to Nome.
items.areas: Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Eastern Norton Sound and Nulato Hills

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 22 at 2:11PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:

southeast towards mainland Alaska. This front will likely bring
chances of precipitation along higher terrain beginning Thursday.
